question:
Choose the option that has the same relationship with the third term as the second term has with the first.

 

QUIC:17210903 ::FILL:?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 6091212.

GIVEN

• QUIC : 17210903 :: FILL : ?

SOLUTION

• Each letter is replaced by its position in the English alphabet, written as a two-digit number: Q = 17, U = 21, I = 09, C = 03. So QUIC = 17 21 09 03 = 17210903.

• Apply the same rule to FILL: F = 6 (06), I = 9 (09), L = 12, L = 12. So FILL = 06 09 12 12.

• Written without the leading zero of the first number, this is 6091212.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Alphabet positions to remember: A = 1, E = 5, I = 9, M = 13, Q = 17, U = 21, Y = 25 (every 4th letter) and F = 6, L = 12. Write each position in the order of the letters.

NOTE

• Option 2 (9061212) is wrong: it begins with 9 and 06, which is the order of the letters I and F reversed.

• Option 3 (5101212) is wrong: 5 and 10 are the positions of E and J, not F and I.

• Option 4 (6081212) is wrong: 08 is the position of H, not I.

• (Flagged: the question shows the first term as 17210903, with two-digit numbers, whereas the key 6091212 omits the leading zero of F = 06. It is the only option that matches 6, 9, 12, 12, so the PDF key is kept.)

question: Fill in the blank: A, E, I, M, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Q.

GIVEN

• Series: A, E, I, M, ?

SOLUTION

• Positions of the letters: A = 1, E = 5, I = 9, M = 13.

• The difference between the terms is +4 each time (1 → 5 → 9 → 13).

• The next term = 13 + 4 = 17, which is the letter Q.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• The series skips three letters each time: A (BCD) E (FGH) I (JKL) M (NOP) Q.

NOTE

• Option 2 (R) is wrong: R is position 18, which would need a step of +5.

• Option 3 (S) is wrong: S is position 19, which would need a step of +6.

• Option 4 (T) is wrong: T is position 20, which would need a step of +7.

• A, E, I, O, U are vowels, but this series follows the +4 pattern and not the vowels, which is why M and Q appear.

question: No birds are mammals. Some birds are crows. Which of the following is true?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. No crow is a mammal.

GIVEN

• Statement 1: No birds are mammals (E-type). Statement 2: Some birds are crows (I-type).

SOLUTION

• Convert the second statement: Some birds are crows → Some crows are birds.

• Combine with "No birds are mammals": the crows that are birds cannot be mammals. So the conclusion is that crows are not mammals (E + I → O*: "Some crows are not mammals", which agrees with "No crow is a mammal" when we also use the common fact that a crow is a bird).

• Option 2 (No crow is a mammal) is the statement consistent with the given information. ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Rule: No birds are mammals + Some birds are crows → Some crows are not mammals. Among the options, the only one that agrees with this (and is not contradicted by the statements) is "No crow is a mammal".

NOTE

• Option 1 (Some crows are mammals) is wrong: crows that are birds cannot be mammals, so it contradicts the first statement.

• Option 3 (All birds are crows) is wrong: only some birds are crows.

• Option 4 (All mammals are birds) is wrong: no bird is a mammal, so no mammal is a bird.

• (Flagged: strictly, the statements give only "Some crows are not mammals". The key "No crow is a mammal" also uses the common fact that all crows are birds. The PDF key, Option 2, is kept.)

question:
Statements:

1. All students are boys.

2. Some boys are players.

Conclusions:

I. Some students are players.

II. All boys are students.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Neither I nor II follows.

GIVEN

• Statement 1: All students are boys (A). Statement 2: Some boys are players (I).

SOLUTION

• Venn diagram: draw "students" completely inside "boys". Draw "players" so that it overlaps "boys".

• Conclusion I (Some students are players): the overlap of boys and players may lie entirely outside the "students" circle (students are only part of boys). So it is not definite. Does not follow.

• Conclusion II (All boys are students): the statement says "All students are boys", and its converse is only "Some boys are students". So "All boys are students" does not follow.

• Neither conclusion follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• A + I gives no conclusion. And the converse of an A-statement is I-type ("All S are B" → "Some B are S"), never A-type.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only I follows) is wrong: students may not overlap players at all.

• Option 2 (Only II follows) is wrong: boys can be more than the students.

• Option 3 (Both I and II follow) is wrong: neither is definite.

• Remember: All A are B does not mean All B are A.

question: All dogs are animals. Some dogs are black. Which of the following conclusions can be drawn?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Some dogs are animals.

GIVEN

• Statement 1: All dogs are animals (A). Statement 2: Some dogs are black (I).

SOLUTION

• "All dogs are animals" directly gives "Some dogs are animals" (A → I by implication). ✓

• "Some dogs are black" gives "Some black things are dogs" by conversion (I → I). ✓

• Combining both: dogs lie inside animals and some dogs are black, so "Some animals are black" also holds (A + I → I). ✓

• "All dogs are black" does not follow, because only some dogs are black. ✗

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Rules: A → I (implication); I → I (conversion); A + I → I (some animals are black). The only option that cannot be drawn is the universal "All dogs are black".

NOTE

• Option 2 (All dogs are black) is wrong: the statement says that only some dogs are black.

• (Flagged: Options 1, 3 and 4 are all logically valid conclusions of the two statements, so the question has more than one valid option. The PDF key is Option 1 (the most direct one), and it is kept. Please check this question against the original paper.)

question: If TABLE = 65 66 69 76 84, what will be the reverse-coded value of CHAIR?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 82 73 65 72 67.

GIVEN

• TABLE = 65 66 69 76 84 (these are the ASCII values of the letters A = 65, B = 66, E = 69, L = 76, T = 84).

SOLUTION

• Find the code of each letter of CHAIR: C = 67, H = 72, A = 65, I = 73, R = 82. In the order of the word this is 67 72 65 73 82.

• "Reverse-coded" means the codes are written in the reverse order of the letters: R, I, A, H, C = 82, 73, 65, 72, 67.

• So the reverse-coded value of CHAIR is 82 73 65 72 67.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• ASCII codes of capital letters: A = 65, B = 66, C = 67, … Z = 90. So the code of any letter = 64 + its position (C = 64 + 3 = 67, H = 64 + 8 = 72, R = 64 + 18 = 82).

NOTE

• Option 2 (67 72 65 73 82) is wrong: it is the forward code of CHAIR, not the reverse.

• Option 3 (83 72 66 72 65) and Option 4 (66 74 63 72 86) are wrong: they contain codes that do not belong to the letters of CHAIR (for example 83 = S and 66 = B).

• (Flagged: in the example, the numbers 65 66 69 76 84 are the codes of the letters of TABLE arranged alphabetically (A, B, E, L, T), while the key reverses the letters of CHAIR. The example and the key do not follow exactly the same rule. The PDF key, Option 1, is kept.)

question:
Six friends – J, K, L, M, N, and O – are sitting in a straight line.

M is sitting to the immediate left of J.

K is not sitting at the ends.

L is sitting second from the left.

Only one person sits between K and N.

Who is sitting to the immediate right of K?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. M.

GIVEN

• Six friends J, K, L, M, N and O sit in a line. M is immediately left of J. K is not at either end. L is second from the left. Only one person sits between K and N. We have to find who is immediately to the right of K.

SOLUTION

• Number the seats 1 to 6 from the left. L is at seat 2.

• M is immediately left of J, so M and J take two adjacent seats (M first). Seats 1–2 are not possible (seat 2 is L), so the pair is at (3, 4), (4, 5) or (5, 6).

• K is not at the ends and L holds seat 2, so K is at 3, 4 or 5.

• Pair at (3, 4): K must be at 5, and N would be at 3 or 7, which is not possible. ✗

• Pair at (4, 5): K = 3, and with one person between K and N, N = 1 (seat 5 is J). O takes seat 6. Arrangement: N, L, K, M, J, O. ✓

• Pair at (5, 6): K = 3 (K = 4 does not work), N = 1, and O takes seat 4. Arrangement: N, L, K, O, M, J.

• In the first arrangement, the person to the immediate right of K is M.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Fix the sure positions first (L = 2, K in the middle seats). Then place the pair (M J) and use "one person between K and N" to place N at seat 1.

NOTE

• Option 2 (O) is wrong in the keyed arrangement (N, L, K, M, J, O), where the person on the right of K is M.

• Option 3 (J) is wrong: J sits to the immediate right of M, not of K.

• Option 4 (L) is wrong: L sits to the immediate left of K.

• (Flagged: a second arrangement, N, L, K, O, M, J, also satisfies every condition, and in it O sits to the right of K. So the question does not fix a single answer. The PDF key, Option 1 (M), is kept. Please check this item against the original paper.)

question:
Statement:

"The government has decided to increase the tax on luxury items to boost revenue."

 

Inferences:

I. The government is facing a budget deficit.

II. Luxury items are considered non-essential goods.
option_4: Neither inference I nor II follows.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Only inference II follows..

GIVEN

• Statement: The government has decided to increase the tax on luxury items to boost revenue.

SOLUTION

• Inference I (The government is facing a budget deficit): the statement only says that the government wants to boost its revenue. It does not say that there is a deficit. The government may want more revenue for other reasons too. Does not follow.

• Inference II (Luxury items are considered non-essential goods): a tax is normally put on luxury items because they are non-essential, so that the burden falls less on the poor. This follows from the idea of "luxury" itself. Follows.

• Hence only inference II follows.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Check whether the inference is directly based on the words of the statement. "Luxury" means non-essential, so II is true by meaning. "Deficit" is a new fact that is not mentioned in the statement.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Only inference I follows) is wrong: a deficit is not mentioned, and I does not follow.

• Option 3 (Both inferences follow) is wrong: inference I does not follow.

• Option 4 (Neither inference I nor II follows) is wrong: inference II follows from the meaning of luxury items.

• (Flagged: inference II depends partly on the meaning of the word "luxury", so it can be argued as an assumption. The PDF key, Option 2, is kept.)

question: You are preparing for an important exam, but your friend needs urgent help with a personal problem. What will you do?
option_1: Help your friend and postpone your study.
option_2: Ignore your friend and continue studying.
option_3: Listen to your friend briefly and suggest a solution, then return to study.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Listen to your friend briefly and suggest a solution, then return to study..

GIVEN

• A situation with two duties: preparing for an important exam, and helping a friend with an urgent personal problem.

SOLUTION

• The best action should balance both duties: give the friend the support he or she needs without harming one's own preparation.

• Listening briefly, suggesting a solution and then returning to study does exactly this. ✓

• So the best option is Option 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• In situation-judgement questions, choose the balanced, practical and responsible option. Reject extreme options (ignore completely, cancel, give up everything).

NOTE

• Option 1 (Help your friend and postpone your study) is wrong: it gives up the exam preparation completely for the friend, which is an extreme step.

• Option 2 (Ignore your friend and continue studying) is wrong: it shows no concern for a friend in need.

• Option 4 (Cancel the exam) is wrong: it is an extreme step with a heavy loss and is not needed.

• A good decision in such cases uses time management and empathy together.

question: How many English words can be formed using any 4 letters of the word "RATED", without repeating any of the letters?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. More than 6.

GIVEN

• Word: RATED (letters R, A, T, E, D). Words of 4 letters are to be formed without repeating any letter.

SOLUTION

• Try the combinations of 4 letters from R, A, T, E, D and look for meaningful words:

• DATE, RATE, TEAR, TARE, DART, DEAR, DARE, READ, TRAD, RATED minus a letter (the above words).

• Counting the common English words alone: DATE, RATE, TEAR, TARE, DART, DEAR, DARE, READ = 8 words, which is more than 6.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Pick the vowels A and E and combine them with two consonants out of R, T, D. Pairs (R, T), (R, D), (T, D) can be arranged to give many words (RATE, TEAR, DARE, DEAR, READ, DATE, DART, TARE).

NOTE

• Option 1 (4), Option 2 (5) and Option 3 (6) are wrong: at least 8 common words can be formed, as listed above.

• In word formation questions, count carefully; common words like DATE, RATE, TEAR, DART, DARE, DEAR, READ and TARE are all possible.

question: Which component is not part of emotional intelligence?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Spatial reasoning.

GIVEN

• The components of emotional intelligence (EI) are asked about.

SOLUTION

• According to Daniel Goleman, emotional intelligence has five components: self-awareness, self-regulation, motivation, empathy and social skills.

• Self-regulation, motivation and empathy are parts of EI. ✓

• Spatial reasoning is the ability to think about shapes and objects in space, which is a part of cognitive (logical) intelligence and not of emotional intelligence.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Emotional intelligence deals with feelings and relationships. Anything that deals with shapes, numbers or logic is not a part of it.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Self-regulation) is wrong: it is the ability to control one's emotions, a component of EI.

• Option 2 (Motivation) is wrong: it is the inner drive to achieve goals, a component of EI.

• Option 4 (Empathy) is wrong: it is understanding the feelings of others, a component of EI.

• Spatial reasoning is part of Howard Gardner's "spatial intelligence" among the multiple intelligences.

question: An emotionally intelligent employee receives criticism from their manager. What would be the best way to respond?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Accept feedback calmly and improve.

GIVEN

• An emotionally intelligent employee gets criticism from the manager. The best response is asked.

SOLUTION

• An emotionally intelligent person manages his or her emotions, listens and learns from feedback.

• Accepting the feedback calmly and working to improve is the response that shows self-regulation and maturity. ✓

• So the best way is Option 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Choose the calm, constructive and growth-oriented response. Options with anger, escape or neglect are wrong.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Get angry and argue back) is wrong: it shows a lack of self-control.

• Option 2 (Quit the job immediately) is wrong: it is an impulsive reaction and not a solution.

• Option 4 (Ignore the manager completely) is wrong: it shows disrespect and a refusal to learn.

• The EI skills used here are self-regulation, self-awareness and social skills.

question: In a certain code language, if "LOWERCASE" is written as "12152351831195", then how will "UPPERCASE" be written in the same code?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 21161651831195.

GIVEN

• LOWERCASE = 12152351831195. Find the code of UPPERCASE.

SOLUTION

• Each letter is replaced by its position in the alphabet: L = 12, O = 15, W = 23, E = 5, R = 18, C = 3, A = 1, S = 19, E = 5.

• Joining them: 12 15 23 5 18 3 1 19 5 = 12152351831195 ✓.

• UPPERCASE: U = 21, P = 16, P = 16, E = 5, R = 18, C = 3, A = 1, S = 19, E = 5.

• Joining: 21 16 16 5 18 3 1 19 5 = 21161651831195.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Only the first three letters change (LOW → UPP). The remaining letters ERCASE have the same code 5 18 3 1 19 5. So the code is 21 16 16 followed by 51831195.

NOTE

• Option 2 (21171751831185) is wrong: P = 16 and not 17, and the tail 1 18 5 is not the code for "ASE".

• Option 3 (21161651931175) is wrong: after 21 16 16 5, the number 19 is used where R = 18 is needed, and the ending is wrong.

• Option 4 (21161661831195) is wrong: it contains 6 in place of 5 for the letter E.

• Positions: E = 5, R = 18, C = 3, A = 1, S = 19, P = 16, U = 21.

question: Choose the pair that follows the same relationship as "Sun : Light"
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Fire : Heat.

GIVEN

• Sun : Light

SOLUTION

• The Sun is a natural source that gives out (produces) light. So the relation is "source : what it gives".

• Fire gives out heat, so Fire : Heat has the same relation. ✓

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Frame a sentence: "The Sun gives out light" → "Fire gives out heat". Test each option with the same sentence.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Air : Fan) is wrong: a fan moves the air, but air is not a source of a fan. The relation is different.

• Option 2 (Bulb : Electricity) is wrong: a bulb uses electricity (the reverse relation); the bulb gives light.

• Option 4 (Moon : Cold) is wrong: the Moon does not produce cold; it reflects sunlight.

question:
Complete the analogy by picking the word that reflects the same relationship as the given pair.

VDHJU : WEGKV :: SKGTN : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. TLFUO.

GIVEN

• VDHJU : WEGKV :: SKGTN : ?

SOLUTION

• Compare the letters of the first pair: V → W (+1), D → E (+1), H → G (–1), J → K (+1), U → V (+1). So the pattern is +1, +1, –1, +1, +1.

• Apply the same pattern to SKGTN: S + 1 = T, K + 1 = L, G – 1 = F, T + 1 = U, N + 1 = O.

• So the answer is TLFUO.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

• Write the sign pattern above the letters (+ + – + +). Only the third letter moves backward, so the third letter of the answer is F (G – 1), which already matches only Option 3 (TLFUO).

NOTE

• Option 1 (TFLNO) is wrong: the second letter should be L (K + 1), not F.

• Option 2 (TFNLO) is wrong: the second letter should be L, not F, and the third and fourth letters are also wrong.

question:
Find the next term in the given number series:

Series: 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 47.

GIVEN

• Series: 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, ?

SOLUTION

• Each term is the sum of the two terms before it: 3 + 4 = 7; 4 + 7 = 11; 7 + 11 = 18; 11 + 18 = 29.

• So the next term = 18 + 29 = 47.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• When the differences (1, 3, 4, 7, 11, 18) are the same as the series itself, the series is of the Fibonacci type (a Lucas series). Add the last two terms.

NOTE

• Option 1 (56) is wrong: it does not equal 18 + 29.

• Option 2 (52) is wrong: it does not equal 18 + 29.

• Option 3 (45) is wrong: it is 29 + 16, and 16 is not the previous term.

• Lucas series: 2, 1, 3, 4, 7, 11, 18, 29, 47, 76, … Fibonacci series: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, …

question: A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a circle facing the centre. A sits fourth to the right of H. A sits second to the left of F. C is not a neighbour of F and B. D sits third to the right of C. H never sits next to G. Who is third to the right of F?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. E.

GIVEN

• Eight persons A to H sit around a circle facing the centre. A is 4th to the right of H. A is 2nd to the left of F. C is not a neighbour of F and B. D is 3rd to the right of C. H never sits next to G.

SOLUTION

• (Facing the centre, "right" is taken as anticlockwise. Number the seats 0 to 7 in the direction of "right".)

• Put H at seat 0. A is 4th to the right of H, so A is at seat 4. A is 2nd to the left of F, so F is 2 seats to the right of A: F is at seat 6.

• D is 3rd to the right of C. The free seats are 1, 2, 3, 5, 7. Possible (C, D) pairs: C = 2 and D = 5, or C = 7 and D = 2. C = 7 is next to F (seat 6), which is not allowed. So C = 2 and D = 5.

• C is not a neighbour of B, so B is not at seat 1 or 3. B is at seat 7 (the remaining seats are 1, 3, 7).

• H (seat 0) does not sit next to G, so G is not at seat 1 or 7. G is at seat 3 and E is at seat 1.

• Seating (0 to 7): H, E, C, G, A, D, F, B.

• The 3rd to the right of F (seat 6) is seat 9 – 8 = 1, which is E.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Start with the two fixed relations (H–A opposite, F two seats from A). Then use "D is 3rd to the right of C" to find the only valid pair (C, D) that does not make C a neighbour of F.

NOTE

• Option 1 (H) is wrong: H is at seat 0, which is 2 seats to the right of F, not 3.

• Option 2 (B) is wrong: B is at seat 7, which is the 1st to the right of F.

• Option 4 (G) is wrong: G is at seat 3, which is the 5th to the right of F.

• Circular arrangement rule: facing the centre, the person on your right side is in the anticlockwise direction.

question: A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H are sitting around a circle facing the centre. A sits fourth to the right of H. A sits second to the left of F. C is not a neighbour of F and B. D sits third to the right of C. H never sits next to G. Who is sitting between B & D?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. F.

GIVEN

• The same arrangement as in the previous question (8 persons around a circle).

SOLUTION

• B is at seat 7 and D is at seat 5. The person sitting between them is at seat 6, which is F.

question:
Which interchange of signs will correct the equation?

35 + 7 × 5 ÷ 5 − 6 = 24
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ÷ and +.

GIVEN

• Equation: 35 + 7 × 5 ÷ 5 − 6 = 24

SOLUTION

• Test Option 3 (interchange ÷ and +): 35 ÷ 7 × 5 + 5 − 6.

• Apply BODMAS: 35 ÷ 7 = 5; 5 × 5 = 25; 25 + 5 = 30; 30 – 6 = 24 ✓.

• So the correct interchange is ÷ and +.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• 35 divided by 7 gives a neat 5 and 35 is a multiple of 7, so try ÷ at that place. Then 5 × 5 = 25 and 25 + 5 – 6 = 24.

NOTE

• Option 1 (× and –): 35 + 7 – 5 ÷ 5 × 6 = 35 + 7 – 6 = 36, not 24.

• Option 2 (+ and ×): 35 × 7 + 5 ÷ 5 − 6 = 245 + 1 – 6 = 240, not 24.

• Option 4 (– and ÷): 35 + 7 × 5 – 5 ÷ 6 = 35 + 35 – 0.83 = 69.17, not 24.

• Always apply BODMAS after interchanging the signs.

question:
What is the next set of letters in the series?

STU,PRT,MPS,JNR,?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. GLQ.

GIVEN

• Series: STU, PRT, MPS, JNR, ?

SOLUTION

• First letters: S, P, M, J → each moves –3 (S → P → M → J → G).

• Second letters: T, R, P, N → each moves –2 (T → R → P → N → L).

• Third letters: U, T, S, R → each moves –1 (U → T → S → R → Q).

• So the next term is GLQ.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Treat the three positions as three series with steps of –3, –2 and –1. Next term: (J – 3)(N – 2)(R – 1) = G L Q.

NOTE

• Option 1 (GKO) is wrong: the second and third letters should be L and Q.

• Option 3 (GLS) is wrong: the third letter should be Q (R – 1), not S.

• Option 4 (GUQ) is wrong: the second letter should be L (N – 2), not U.

question:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the below equation mathematically correct?

42 + 12 ÷ 24 × 84 - 14 = 91
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. + and ×.

GIVEN

• Equation: 42 + 12 ÷ 24 × 84 – 14 = 91

SOLUTION

• Test Option 1 (interchange + and ×): 42 × 12 ÷ 24 + 84 – 14.

• 42 × 12 = 504; 504 ÷ 24 = 21; 21 + 84 = 105; 105 – 14 = 91 ✓.

• So the correct interchange is + and ×.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Since 24 divides 12 × 42 exactly (the result is 21), the first term should be 42 × 12 ÷ 24. Then 21 + 84 – 14 = 91.

NOTE

• Option 2 (÷ and –): 42 + 12 – 24 × 84 ÷ 14 = 42 + 12 – 144 = –90, not 91.

• Option 3 (– and +): 42 – 12 ÷ 24 × 84 + 14 = 42 – 42 + 14 = 14, not 91.

• Option 4 (× and ÷): 42 + 12 × 24 ÷ 84 – 14 = 42 + 3.43 – 14 = 31.43, not 91.

question: Which of the following options replaces the '?' in the image given?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 14.

GIVEN

• Three figures with four numbers each. Figure 1: top 46, left 19, right 27, bottom 73. Figure 2: top 54, left 33, right 21, bottom 75. Figure 3: top 49, left ?, right 35, bottom 84.

SOLUTION

question: A man is facing east. He turns 90° to his right, then 180° to his left, and finally 90° to his left again. Which direction is he facing now?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. West.

GIVEN

• Start: facing East. Turns: 90° right, then 180° left, then 90° left.

SOLUTION

• East, turn 90° to the right (clockwise): South.

• South, turn 180° to the left: North (a 180° turn gives the opposite direction).

• North, turn 90° to the left (anticlockwise): West.

• So he is finally facing West.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Take right = +90° and left = –90° (clockwise positive): +90 – 180 – 90 = –180°. East (90° on the compass) minus 180° gives 270°, which is West.

NOTE

• Option 1 (North) is wrong: North is the direction after the second turn only.

• Option 2 (South) is wrong: South is the direction after the first turn only.

• Option 3 (East) is wrong: he would face East only if the net turn were 0° or 360°; here it is 180°.

• Compass: N = 0°, E = 90°, S = 180°, W = 270°. Right turn = clockwise, left turn = anticlockwise.

question: In a certain code, 'BASKET' is '5$#%&1' and 'TRIED' is '1@&2'*'. How is 'SKIRT' coded?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. #%@*1.

GIVEN

• BASKET = 5 $ # % & 1 and TRIED = 1 @ & 2 ' * (as printed in the paper). SKIRT = ?

SOLUTION

• From BASKET: B = 5, A = $, S = #, K = %, E = &, T = 1.

• From TRIED: T = 1, and the remaining symbols give R, I and D. The code of SKIRT needs only S, K, I, R and T, so I and R must be found: the symbols @ and * stand for I and R. Using the key, the only option that fits the pattern S K I R T = # % @ * 1 is Option 1.

• S = #, K = %, I = @, R = *, T = 1, so SKIRT = #%@*1.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Every option starts with #% (S, K) and ends with 1 or 2 (T = 1, so the last symbol must be 1). Only the 3rd and 4th symbols (I, R) need checking, and they are @ and * in that order.

NOTE

• Option 2 (#%@&1) is wrong: & is the code of E, not R.

• Option 3 (#%*&1) is wrong: the 3rd and 4th symbols are & and *, which do not stand for I and R.

• Option 4 (#%@*2) is wrong: the last letter T is coded 1, not 2 (2 is the code of D).

• Source note: the coded form of TRIED is printed in the paper as '1@&2'*', with the symbols out of order; the key in the PDF (Option 1) is consistent with I = @ and R = *.

question: In a certain code language, the word FASHION is written as FOIHSAN. Using the same rule, how would the word PROBLEM be written?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. PELBORM.

GIVEN

• FASHION → FOIHSAN. PROBLEM → ?

SOLUTION

• Positions in FASHION: F A S H I O N (1 to 7). In FOIHSAN: F O I H S A N.

• The first letter F and the last letter N stay in place. The middle five letters A S H I O become O I H S A, which is their reverse.

• Apply this to PROBLEM: P stays, M stays, and the middle ROBLE is reversed to ELBOR.

• So PROBLEM becomes P + ELBOR + M = PELBORM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• "First and last fixed, middle reversed": keep P and M, reverse ROBLE.

NOTE

• Option 1 (PMELBOR) is wrong: M is moved to the second place, but the last letter must stay last.

• Option 2 (ROBLEMP) is wrong: the first letter P is shifted to the end.

• Option 4 (RPBOELM) is wrong: the letters are only shuffled, with no reversal of the middle letters.

question: Which Supreme Court ruling recognized transgender individuals as the ‘third gender’ in India?

• Option 4 (Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India, 2018) is wrong: it decriminalised consensual same-sex relations by reading down Section 377 of the IPC.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• NALSA stands for National Legal Services Authority. The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act was passed in 2019.

 

• Important cases to remember: Kesavananda Bharati (1973, basic structure), Maneka Gandhi (1978, Article 21), Shayara Bano (2017, triple talaq).

question: Which organization is responsible for enforcing criminal laws in India?

EXTRA FACTS

 

• The three organs of the government: Legislature (makes laws), Executive (implements laws; the police fall here) and Judiciary (interprets laws and delivers justice).

 

• Police and Public Order are State List subjects (Seventh Schedule). Since 2024, the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS) and Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA) have replaced the IPC, CrPC and Evidence Act.

 

FLAG

question: Which dance form integrates "vachika abhinaya" (spoken word) along with expressive dance?

question: Which of the following is another name for Buddha Purnima?
solution_text:

ANSWER

 

• Vesak (also written Vesakha or Wesak) is another name of Buddha Purnima.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• Buddha Purnima is observed on the full-moon day of the month of Vaisakha (April–May). It marks the birth, enlightenment (Bodh Gaya) and Mahaparinirvana (Kushinagar) of Gautama Buddha. In Southeast Asia it is called Vesak.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

• Option 3 (Pavaran) is wrong: Pavarana marks the end of the Buddhist rainy-season retreat (Vassa).

 

• Option 4 (Magha Puja) is wrong: it commemorates the gathering of 1,250 disciples of the Buddha, on the full moon of the month of Magha (Feb–March).

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• The UN recognises Vesak as an international day (since 1999/2000). The Buddha was born at Lumbini (Nepal) in 563 BCE (traditional dating).

 

• Four major Buddhist pilgrimage sites: Lumbini, Bodh Gaya, Sarnath, Kushinagar.

 

• Source note: in the PDF, a page break falls between option 2 and option 3; the question has four options.

question: What are the specialized receptors that detect the sensation of taste called?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gustatory ones.

 

ANSWER

 

• Gustatory ones (gustatory receptors, or taste buds).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• The sense of taste is called gustation. Taste receptor cells grouped in taste buds, found mainly on the tongue's papillae, detect the five basic tastes: sweet, sour, salty, bitter and umami.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

 

• Option 1 (Olfactory) is wrong: olfactory receptors are in the nasal cavity and detect smell.

 

• Option 2 (Dendrite tips) is wrong: these are parts of a neuron and are not the specialised taste receptors.

 

• Option 3 (Sensory nerves) is wrong: sensory nerves only carry the signals to the brain; the receptors are the taste cells.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• Taste signals travel via the facial (VII), glossopharyngeal (IX) and vagus (X) cranial nerves. Taste buds on the tongue: about 2,000 to 8,000.

 

• Receptors: photoreceptors (eye), mechanoreceptors (ear, skin), thermoreceptors (temperature), nociceptors (pain), chemoreceptors (taste, smell).

question: Inflation refers to:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Increase in general price level.

 

ANSWER

 

• Increase in general price level.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

EXPLANATION

 

• Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level of goods and services over time, which lowers the purchasing power of money. It is measured by the CPI and WPI.

 

WHY THE OTHERS ARE WRONG

 

• Option 2 (Increase in employment) is wrong: employment growth is an economic indicator but not the definition of inflation.

 

• Option 3 (Decrease in money supply) is wrong: a lower money supply tends to reduce prices (it is a tool against inflation).

 

• Option 4 (Decrease in general price level) is wrong: this is deflation.

 

EXTRA FACTS

 

• Types: demand-pull, cost-push, structural; disinflation is a fall in the rate of inflation; stagflation is high inflation with high unemployment.

 

• India's inflation targeting: 4 per cent with a band of ±2 per cent (RBI Act amendment, 2016); the CPI is the target measure.

question: India's development of its own Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV) represents a significant achievement in space technology. Which strategic advantage does this capability provide to the country?

option_3: Guarantees Indian satellites more advanced than others
option_4: Replaces need for ground stations like NRSC
solution_text:

ANSWER

 

• Reduces dependence on foreign launchers; builds indigenous satellite capacity.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

question: Two alloys P and Q are made of metals X, Y, and Z. In P, the ratio of masses of X:Y:Z is 2:3:5, and in Q, it is 3:5:7. If 12 kg of P and 18 kg of Q are melted together to form a new alloy R, find the ratio of masses of X:Y:Z in R.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 5:8:12.

GIVEN

• P: X : Y : Z = 2 : 3 : 5 (total 10 parts). Q: X : Y : Z = 3 : 5 : 7 (total 15 parts). 12 kg of P and 18 kg of Q are melted.

SOLUTION

• In 12 kg of P (1 part = 1.2 kg): X = 2.4, Y = 3.6, Z = 6 kg.

• In 18 kg of Q (1 part = 1.2 kg): X = 3.6, Y = 6, Z = 8.4 kg.

• In R: X = 2.4 + 3.6 = 6 kg; Y = 3.6 + 6 = 9.6 kg; Z = 6 + 8.4 = 14.4 kg.

• Ratio = 6 : 9.6 : 14.4. Divide each by 1.2: 5 : 8 : 12. So the answer is 5 : 8 : 12.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Both alloys have a part value of 1.2 kg, so you can add the ratio terms directly: (2 + 3) : (3 + 5) : (5 + 7) = 5 : 8 : 12.

NOTE

• Option 2 (13 : 22 : 32) is wrong: its terms add up to 67, which is not a multiple that fits the 30 kg total with these masses.

• Option 3 (12 : 21 : 31) is wrong: the Y and Z terms do not match 9.6 and 14.4 in proportion to X = 6.

• Option 4 (15 : 25 : 35) is wrong: it reduces to 3 : 5 : 7, which is the ratio of Q alone. (The PDF shows Option 3 as a wrong selection.)

• Rule: when you mix alloys, convert each to actual masses, add metal-wise and then reduce the ratio.

question: What is the missing number in the equation: 8 + __ × 3 = 20?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• 8 + __ × 3 = 20

SOLUTION

• By BODMAS, multiplication is done before addition: 8 + (__ × 3) = 20.

• So  × 3 = 20 – 8 = 12, and  = 12 ÷ 3 = 4.

• Check: 8 + 4 × 3 = 8 + 12 = 20 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Substitute the options: 8 + 4 × 3 = 20 straight away.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2): 8 + 2 × 3 = 14, not 20.

• Option 3 (6): 8 + 6 × 3 = 26, not 20.

• Option 4 (5): 8 + 5 × 3 = 23, not 20. (Taking (8 + 5) × 3 = 39 is also wrong; the multiplication comes first.)

• BODMAS: Brackets, Orders, Division/Multiplication, Addition/Subtraction.

question: Two twins, Alpha and Beta, were asked to calculate the square of numbers symmetrically placed around a mysterious number x. According to given problem => (x + 3)² - (x - 3)² ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 12x.

GIVEN

• (x + 3)² – (x – 3)²

SOLUTION

• Use the identity (a + b)² – (a – b)² = 4ab, with a = x and b = 3.

• So the result is 4 × x × 3 = 12x.

• Check by expanding: (x² + 6x + 9) – (x² – 6x + 9) = 12x ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• (a + b)² – (a – b)² = 4ab. Put x = 1 to check: 16 – 4 = 12, and only 12x gives 12.

NOTE

• Option 1 (6x) is wrong: this is only one of the middle terms (+6x), not the difference of the two expansions.

• Option 2 (9x) is wrong: the constant 9 cancels out and there is no 9x term.

• Option 4 (18x) is wrong: with x = 1 it gives 18, but the actual value is 12.

• Related identity: (a + b)² + (a – b)² = 2(a² + b²).

question: A cyclist travels a distance of 36 km in 9 hours. What is his average speed?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 4 km/h.

GIVEN

• Distance = 36 km, time = 9 hours.

SOLUTION

• Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 36 ÷ 9 = 4 km/h.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• 36 = 4 × 9, so the speed is 4 km/h directly.

NOTE

• Option 2 (6 km/h) is wrong: it would cover 6 × 9 = 54 km in 9 hours.

• Option 3 (5 km/h) is wrong: it would cover 5 × 9 = 45 km.

• Option 4 (7 km/h) is wrong: it would cover 7 × 9 = 63 km.

• Formula: speed = distance ÷ time; to convert km/h to m/s multiply by 5/18.

question: In a 104-litre solution of milk and water where the milk to water ratio is 8:5, what quantity of water should be mixed in to obtain a final ratio of 4:3?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. 8 L.

GIVEN

• Total = 104 L; milk : water = 8 : 5. Required final ratio milk : water = 4 : 3.

SOLUTION

• Milk = 104 × 8/13 = 64 L and water = 104 × 5/13 = 40 L.

• Let x litres of water be added: 64 / (40 + x) = 4/3.

• 4(40 + x) = 192, so 40 + x = 48, giving x = 8 L.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

SHORT TRICK

• Milk stays the same at 64 L, which is 4 parts, so 1 part = 16 L and 3 parts = 48 L of water. Added water = 48 – 40 = 8 L.

NOTE

• Option 2 (7 L): the water becomes 47 L and the ratio is 64 : 47, not 4 : 3.

• Option 3 (6 L): the water becomes 46 L and the ratio is 64 : 46, not 4 : 3.

• Option 4 (9 L): the water becomes 49 L and the ratio is 64 : 49, not 4 : 3.

• Rule: when only one component is added, the other component stays constant; use it as the base of the new ratio.

question: The sum of the length and breadth of a rectangle is 28 cm and sum of the perimeters of the rectangle and a square is 96 cm. Find the diagonal of square.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 10√2 cm.

GIVEN

• l + b = 28 cm; perimeter of rectangle + perimeter of square = 96 cm.

SOLUTION

• Perimeter of the rectangle = 2(l + b) = 2 × 28 = 56 cm.

• Perimeter of the square = 96 – 56 = 40 cm, so its side = 40 ÷ 4 = 10 cm.

• Diagonal of a square = side × √2 = 10√2 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Diagonal of a square = a√2. Find the side from the perimeter (40 ÷ 4 = 10).

NOTE

• Option 1 (15√2 cm) is wrong: the side would be 15 cm and the perimeter 60 cm, leaving 36 cm for the rectangle, not 56 cm.

• Option 2 (11√2 cm) is wrong: the side would be 11 cm and the perimeter 44 cm.

• Option 4 (12√2 cm) is wrong: the side would be 12 cm and the perimeter 48 cm.

• Formulas: diagonal of a square = a√2; area = d²/2; diagonal of a rectangle = √(l² + b²).

question: Which of the following G.P. series has a common ratio which is not a perfect square?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. 6, 21.6, 77.76, ......

GIVEN

• Four G.P. series. Find the one whose common ratio is not a perfect square.

SOLUTION

• Series 1: r = 4 ÷ 1 = 4 = 2², a perfect square.

• Series 2: r = 18 ÷ 2 = 9 = 3², a perfect square.

• Series 3: r = 2.88 ÷ 2 = 1.44 = (1.2)², a perfect square (and 2.88 × 1.44 = 4.1472).

• Series 4: r = 21.6 ÷ 6 = 3.6, and √3.6 ≈ 1.897 is not a terminating or whole number, so 3.6 is not a perfect square (check: 21.6 × 3.6 = 77.76).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

SHORT TRICK

• Find r = second ÷ first for each series and test whether its square root is a nice number: 4 → 2, 9 → 3, 1.44 → 1.2, 3.6 → no.

NOTE

• Option 1 (1, 4, 16, 64): r = 4 = 2², so it is a perfect square.

• Option 2 (2, 18, 162, 1458): r = 9 = 3², so it is a perfect square.

• Option 3 (2, 2.88, 4.1472): r = 1.44 = 1.2², so it is a perfect square.

• G.P. formulas: nth term = ar^(n–1); sum of n terms = a(rⁿ – 1)/(r – 1).

question: If 2² + 4² + 6² + 8²....................... + 50² = 5525, then find the value of 1² + 2² + 3²............... + 25² = ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 1381.25.

GIVEN

• 2² + 4² + 6² + … + 50² = 5525. Find 1² + 2² + 3² + … + 25².

SOLUTION

• 2² + 4² + … + 50² = (2 × 1)² + (2 × 2)² + … + (2 × 25)² = 4 × (1² + 2² + … + 25²).

• So 4 × (1² + 2² + … + 25²) = 5525.

• 1² + 2² + … + 25² = 5525 ÷ 4 = 1381.25.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• The even squares are 4 times the squares of 1 to 25, so divide by 4: 5525 ÷ 4 = 1381.25.

NOTE

• Option 1 (1340.25), Option 2 (1215.25) and Option 4 (1524.75) are wrong: multiplied by 4 they give 5361, 4861 and 6099, none of which equals 5525.

• Formula: 1² + 2² + … + n² = n(n + 1)(2n + 1)/6. The answer here is obtained from the data given in the question (5525 ÷ 4).

FLAG

• By the standard formula, 1² + … + 25² = 25 × 26 × 51/6 = 5525, and the sum of even squares up to 50² is 22100, not 5525. The question's data are therefore inconsistent with the standard formula; the PDF key (Option 3, 1381.25), which follows the question's data, has been kept.

question: Michael takes a loan from a finance company at a compound interest rate of 8.33% per annum. He agrees to clear the loan in two instalments ₹6,500 at the end of the first year and ₹8,450 at the end of the second year. Assuming the interest is compounded annually, how much interest did Michael pay in total over the two years?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ₹1,750.

GIVEN

• Rate = 8.33% = 1/12 per annum (8⅓%). Instalments: ₹6,500 (end of year 1), ₹8,450 (end of year 2).

SOLUTION

• Let the loan be P. Each year the amount becomes (13/12) of the balance.

• After year 2 the last instalment clears the loan: balance at the end of year 1 (after the first payment) × 13/12 = 8,450.

• So the balance after year 1's payment = 8,450 × 12/13 = 7,800.

• Before the first payment it was 7,800 + 6,500 = 14,300 = P × 13/12, so P = 14,300 × 12/13 = ₹13,200.

• Total paid = 6,500 + 8,450 = 14,950. Interest = 14,950 – 13,200 = ₹1,750.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Work backwards: present value of 8,450 at 1/12 per year is 8,450 × 12/13 = 7,800; plus 6,500 = 14,300; × 12/13 = 13,200. Interest = total paid – loan.

NOTE

• Option 1 (₹1,960), Option 2 (₹1,850) and Option 4 (₹1,820) are wrong: they would need a loan of ₹12,990, ₹13,100 or ₹13,130, which does not satisfy the instalment conditions.

• 8.33% is read as 8⅓% = 1/12, which is the usual SSC convention.

• Rate fractions: 8⅓% = 1/12, 12½% = 1/8, 16⅔% = 1/6, 6¼% = 1/16.

question: After allowing a discount of 20%, the value of an item is Rs. 36,800. If no discount is allowed, then the shopkeeper gain 15%. Find the cost price of the item?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Rs. 40,000.

GIVEN

• Selling price after 20% discount = Rs. 36,800. With no discount (at marked price), the gain is 15%.

SOLUTION

• 80% of the marked price = 36,800, so marked price = 36,800 ÷ 0.8 = Rs. 46,000.

• Marked price = cost price × 115/100, so cost price = 46,000 × 100/115 = Rs. 40,000.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Cost price × 1.15 = marked price; marked price × 0.8 = 36,800. CP = 36,800/(0.8 × 1.15) = 36,800/0.92 = 40,000.

NOTE

• Option 1 (Rs. 42,000): 42,000 × 1.15 = 48,300, not 46,000.

• Option 2 (Rs. 45,000): 45,000 × 1.15 = 51,750, not 46,000.

• Option 4 (Rs. 41,500): 41,500 × 1.15 = 47,725, not 46,000.

• Formula: selling price = marked price × (100 – d)/100; cost price = selling price × 100/(100 + gain%).

question: A container holds a mixture of salt and water in which 8% of the mixture is salt. Some water is evaporated, but the amount of salt remains the same. After 12 litres of water evaporate, the salt concentration rises to 20%. What was the initial volume (in litres) of the salt–water solution?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 20 lit.

GIVEN

• Initial salt = 8% of V. After evaporation of 12 L, volume = V – 12 and salt = 20%.

SOLUTION

• The amount of salt is unchanged: 0.08 V = 0.20 (V – 12).

• 0.08 V = 0.20 V – 2.4, so 0.12 V = 2.4 and V = 20 litres.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Salt is constant, so volume is inversely proportional to the concentration: 8 : 20 = 2 : 5, so the new volume is 2/5 of the initial one. The loss of 3/5 of V equals 12 L, so V = 12 × 5/3 = 20 L.

NOTE

• Option 1 (24 lit): salt = 1.92 L in the remaining 12 L, which is 16%, not 20%.

• Option 2 (18 lit): salt = 1.44 L in the remaining 6 L, which is 24%, not 20%.

• Option 4 (21 lit): salt = 1.68 L in the remaining 9 L, which is about 18.7%, not 20%.

• Rule: in evaporation problems, the solute is constant; use "concentration × volume = constant".

question: A, B and C together start a business by investing a total amount of ₹4.5 lakhs. A invests some amount of money; B invests ₹75,000 more than A and C invests ₹30,000 less than B. After one year the business earns a total profit of ₹16,200, which has to be shared among the partners in the ratio of their investments. Find the profit of C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ₹5,580.

GIVEN

• Total investment = ₹4,50,000. B = A + 75,000; C = B – 30,000. Total profit = ₹16,200.

SOLUTION

• Let A = a. Then B = a + 75,000 and C = a + 75,000 – 30,000 = a + 45,000.

• a + (a + 75,000) + (a + 45,000) = 4,50,000, so 3a = 3,30,000 and a = ₹1,10,000.

• B = ₹1,85,000 and C = ₹1,55,000.

• Ratio A : B : C = 110 : 185 : 155 = 22 : 37 : 31 (total 90 parts).

• C's profit = 16,200 × 31/90 = 180 × 31 = ₹5,580.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• 16,200 ÷ 90 = 180 per part, so C = 31 × 180 = 5,580.

NOTE

• Option 1 (₹4,580) is wrong: it does not equal 31 parts of ₹180.

• Option 2 (₹6,500) is wrong: it is not a whole number of parts (6,500 ÷ 180 is not an integer).

• Option 4 (₹6,540) is wrong: B's profit is 37 × 180 = ₹6,660 and A's is 22 × 180 = ₹3,960; 6,540 matches neither.

• Rule: partners with equal time share profit in the ratio of their investments.

• Source note: in the PDF, a page break falls between option 2 and option 3; the question has four options.

question: Two boats go downstream from point X to point Y. The faster boat covers the distance from X to Y is 1.5 times as fast as the slower boat. It is known that for every hour the slower boat lags behind the faster boat by 12 km. However, if they go up stream then the faster boat covers the distance from Y to X in half the time as the slower boat. Find the speed of the faster boat in still water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 30 kmph.

GIVEN

• Downstream, the faster boat is 1.5 times as fast as the slower boat; the slower boat lags by 12 km every hour. Upstream, the faster boat takes half the time of the slower boat.

SOLUTION

• Let the speed of the faster boat in still water be f, of the slower boat be s, and of the stream be u.

• Downstream: f + u = 1.5 (s + u), and (f + u) – (s + u) = 12, so 0.5 (s + u) = 12, which gives s + u = 24 and f + u = 36.

• Upstream: the faster boat takes half the time, so its speed is double: f – u = 2 (s – u), which gives f + u = 2s. So 36 = 2s and s = 18.

• Then u = 24 – 18 = 6 and f = 36 – 6 = 30 kmph.

• Check: upstream speeds are 30 – 6 = 24 and 18 – 6 = 12; 24 is twice 12 ✓.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• The downstream speed difference is 12 km/h and the ratio is 3 : 2, so the speeds are 36 and 24 downstream. For the upstream ratio of 2 : 1, f + u = 2s gives s = 18, so u = 6 and f = 30.

NOTE

• Option 1 (24 kmph) is wrong: 24 km/h is the slower boat's downstream speed; with f = 24 the stream would be 12 and the slower boat's upstream speed 0.

• Option 3 (28 kmph) is wrong: f = 28 gives u = 8 and s = 16, so the upstream speeds are 20 and 8, a ratio of 2.5 : 1, not 2 : 1.

• Option 4 (42 kmph) is wrong: it would give a negative stream speed (u = –6).

• Formulas: downstream speed = boat + stream; upstream speed = boat – stream; still-water speed = (downstream + upstream)/2.

question: Ravi, Suresh and Mahesh work at a juice unit. Ravi takes 2 hours to extract as much juice as Suresh can extract in 3 hours. Mahesh takes 6 hours to extract as much juice as Ravi extracts in 4 hours. Working together, they fill a storage tank in 6 hours. How long will Mahesh take to fill the tank alone?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 21 hours.

GIVEN

• Ravi's 2 hours of work = Suresh's 3 hours of work. Mahesh's 6 hours = Ravi's 4 hours. All three together fill the tank in 6 hours.

SOLUTION

• Ravi and Suresh: the same work takes 2 h and 3 h, so their efficiencies are in the ratio 3 : 2 (Ravi : Suresh).

• Mahesh and Ravi: the same work takes 6 h and 4 h, so the efficiencies are in the ratio 4 : 6 = 2 : 3 (Mahesh : Ravi).

• So Ravi : Suresh : Mahesh = 3 : 2 : 2, with a total efficiency of 7 units per hour.

• Total work = 7 × 6 = 42 units.

• Mahesh alone = 42 ÷ 2 = 21 hours.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Time and efficiency are inversely proportional. Efficiency 3 : 2 : 2 gives 7 units/hour; total work = 7 × 6 = 42; Mahesh's time = 42 ÷ 2 = 21.

NOTE

• Option 1 (18 hours): Mahesh's rate would have to be 42 ÷ 18 = 7/3 units, which does not match 2.

• Option 2 (14 hours): the rate would be 3 units, which is Ravi's rate, not Mahesh's.

• Option 4 (25 hours): 42 ÷ 25 is not 2 units/hour.

• Rule: work = efficiency × time; with the same work, efficiency ∝ 1/time.

question: A chord of a circle subtends an angle of 40° at a point on the circle. Find the angle subtended by the same chord at a point on the opposite segment.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 140°.

GIVEN

• A chord subtends 40° at a point on the circle (in the major segment).

SOLUTION

• The two points (one on each segment) form a cyclic quadrilateral with the chord.

• In a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles add up to 180°.

• So the angle in the opposite segment = 180° – 40° = 140°.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Angles in the same segment are equal; angles in opposite segments are supplementary: 180° – 40° = 140°.

NOTE

• Option 1 (40°) is wrong: that is the angle at any point in the same segment.

• Option 2 (80°) is wrong: that is the angle at the centre (twice 40°).

• Option 4 (160°) is wrong: there is no circle theorem giving 160°; supplementary angles give 140°.

• Source note: in the PDF, a page break falls after option 3; the question has four options.

question: The smallest number to be added to 697221 to make the sum a perfect square is:
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• Number = 697221.

SOLUTION

• 834² = 695,556 and 835² = 697,225. Since 834² is smaller than 697221, the number lies between 834² and 835².

• The next perfect square is 835² = 697,225.

• Number to be added = 697,225 – 697,221 = 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• √697221 is just below 835. Check 835²: (800 + 35)² = 640,000 + 56,000 + 1,225 = 697,225. The difference is 4.

NOTE

• Option 1 (6): 697227 is not a perfect square (it lies between 835² and 836²).

• Option 3 (8): 697229 is not a perfect square.

• Option 4 (5): 697226 is not a perfect square.

• Squares ending in 5 follow the rule (n5)² = n(n + 1) followed by 25: 83 × 84 = 6972, so 835² = 697225.

question: A number leaves a remainder of 17 when divided by 36. What is the remainder when the same number is divided by 12?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 5.

GIVEN

• Number N leaves remainder 17 when divided by 36.

SOLUTION

• N = 36k + 17 = 36k + 12 + 5 = 12 (3k + 1) + 5.

• So when N is divided by 12, the remainder is 5.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Since 12 is a factor of 36, divide the remainder 17 by 12 directly: 17 ÷ 12 gives remainder 5.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2), Option 3 (3) and Option 4 (7) are wrong: N = 36k + 17 = 12(3k + 1) + 5, so the remainder is always 5 whatever k is. (Test with N = 17: 17 ÷ 12 leaves 5.)

• Rule: if N leaves remainder r on division by D, it leaves remainder (r mod d) on division by any factor d of D.

question: A, B, and C are employed to do a piece of work for ₹529. A and B together are supposed to do 19/23 of the work and B and C together 8/23 of the work. What amount should be paid to A?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. ₹345.

GIVEN

• Total payment = ₹529. A + B = 19/23 of the work; B + C = 8/23 of the work.

SOLUTION

• Total work = A + B + C = 23/23. So C = 23/23 – 19/23 = 4/23.

• B = 8/23 – 4/23 = 4/23.

• A = 19/23 – 4/23 = 15/23.

• A's payment = 529 × 15/23 = 23 × 15 = ₹345.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• A's share = whole – (B + C) = 1 – 8/23 = 15/23. Then 529 ÷ 23 = 23 and 23 × 15 = 345.

NOTE

• Option 1 (₹450) is wrong: it would be 450/529 of the work, which is not 15/23.

• Option 2 (₹275) is wrong: it equals about 11.96/23 of the work, which does not match.

• Option 4 (₹425) is wrong: it equals about 18.5/23 of the work, which does not match.

• B's and C's payments are each 529 × 4/23 = ₹92; the three payments add up to 345 + 92 + 92 = ₹529.

question: Triangles ABC and PQR are similar in the order ABC ~ PQR. If AB = 8 cm, BC = 10 cm, CA = 12 cm and PQ = 12 cm, what is the perimeter of triangle PQR?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 45 cm.

GIVEN

• ABC ~ PQR; AB = 8, BC = 10, CA = 12 (all in cm); PQ = 12 cm.

SOLUTION

• In ABC ~ PQR, AB corresponds to PQ. Ratio = PQ/AB = 12/8 = 3/2.

• Perimeter of ABC = 8 + 10 + 12 = 30 cm.

• Perimeter of PQR = 30 × 3/2 = 45 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• In similar triangles, the ratio of perimeters equals the ratio of corresponding sides: 30 × (12/8) = 45.

NOTE

• Option 1 (36 cm) would need a ratio of 1.2 (36 ÷ 30), but the ratio is 1.5.

• Option 2 (42 cm) would need a ratio of 1.4, but the ratio is 1.5.

• Option 4 (54 cm) would need a ratio of 1.8, but the ratio is 1.5.

• Rules: the ratio of areas of similar triangles = (ratio of sides)²; the ratio of perimeters = ratio of sides.

• Source note: in the PDF, a page break falls between option 1 and option 2; the question has four options.

question: Evaluate: sin²18° + sin² 72° + cos² 36° + cos² 54° + tan15° tan75°.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 3.

GIVEN

• sin²18° + sin²72° + cos²36° + cos²54° + tan15° tan75°

SOLUTION

• sin 72° = cos 18° (since 72° = 90° – 18°), so sin²72° = cos²18°. Then sin²18° + sin²72° = sin²18° + cos²18° = 1.

• cos 54° = sin 36° (since 54° = 90° – 36°), so cos²54° = sin²36°. Then cos²36° + cos²54° = cos²36° + sin²36° = 1.

• tan 75° = cot 15°, so tan15° × tan75° = tan15° × cot15° = 1.

• Total = 1 + 1 + 1 = 3.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Pair up complementary angles (18° + 72° = 90°, 36° + 54° = 90°, 15° + 75° = 90°). Each pair gives 1, so the answer is 3.

NOTE

• Option 1 (2) is wrong: it leaves out the tan15° tan75° term, which is 1.

• Option 2 (5/2) is wrong: it does not follow from any pairing; each pair gives exactly 1.

• Option 4 (4) is wrong: there are only three pairs, so the sum cannot be 4.

• Complementary-angle results: sin(90° – θ) = cos θ, tan(90° – θ) = cot θ, and tan θ × tan(90° – θ) = 1.

question: A rhombus has diagonals 16 cm and 30 cm. Use half-diagonals to find its side and perimeter. What is the perimeter?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 68 cm.

GIVEN

• Diagonals of the rhombus: 16 cm and 30 cm.

SOLUTION

• The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. The half-diagonals are 8 cm and 15 cm.

• Side = √(8² + 15²) = √(64 + 225) = √289 = 17 cm.

• Perimeter = 4 × side = 4 × 17 = 68 cm.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• 8, 15, 17 is a Pythagorean triplet, so the side is 17 cm. Perimeter = 68 cm.

NOTE

• Option 1 (60 cm) is wrong: it equals 4 × 15, using a half-diagonal as the side.

• Option 2 (64 cm) is wrong: it equals 4 × 16, using the full diagonal 16 as the side.

• Option 4 (72 cm) is wrong: it would need a side of 18 cm, but the side is 17 cm.

• Formulas: area of a rhombus = ½ × d₁ × d₂ = 240 cm²; side = ½ √(d₁² + d₂²).

question: The angle of elevation of the top of a tower from a point 30 m away from its base on level ground is 30°. What is the height of the tower?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. 10√3 m.

GIVEN

• Horizontal distance = 30 m; angle of elevation = 30°.

SOLUTION

• tan 30° = height ÷ base, so height = 30 × tan 30° = 30 × (1/√3).

• 30/√3 = (30 × √3)/3 = 10√3 m.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• Use tan 30° = 1/√3 and rationalise: 30/√3 = 10√3 (about 17.3 m).

NOTE

• Option 1 (15√3 m) is wrong: it would need tan θ = 15√3/30 = √3/2, which is not tan 30°.

• Option 2 (30√3 m) is wrong: this is the height if the angle were 60° (30 × tan 60°).

• Option 4 (20 m) is wrong: it would need tan θ = 2/3, which is not tan 30°.

• Standard values: tan 30° = 1/√3, tan 45° = 1, tan 60° = √3.

question: If the sum of the first n natural numbers is 210, find n.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 20.

GIVEN

• 1 + 2 + 3 + … + n = 210.

SOLUTION

• Sum = n(n + 1)/2 = 210, so n(n + 1) = 420.

• 20 × 21 = 420, so n = 20.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• Find two consecutive numbers whose product is 420: 20 × 21.

NOTE

• Option 1 (19): the sum would be 19 × 20/2 = 190.

• Option 3 (21): the sum would be 21 × 22/2 = 231.

• Option 4 (22): the sum would be 22 × 23/2 = 253.

• Formula: sum of the first n natural numbers = n(n + 1)/2; of the first n odd numbers = n²; of the first n even numbers = n(n + 1).

question: Which of the following is an irrational number?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. √7.

GIVEN

• Four numbers; find the irrational one.

SOLUTION

• An irrational number cannot be written as p/q (integers) and its decimal expansion never terminates or repeats.

• √16 = 4, which is an integer (rational). 22/7 is a fraction (rational). 0.25 = 1/4 (rational).

• 7 is not a perfect square, so √7 = 2.6457… is non-terminating and non-repeating: √7 is irrational.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

SHORT TRICK

• The square root of a non-perfect-square natural number is always irrational.

NOTE

• Option 1 (√16) is wrong: it equals 4, a rational number.

• Option 2 (22/7) is wrong: it is a ratio of two integers, hence rational (it is only an approximation of π).

• Option 4 (0.25) is wrong: it is a terminating decimal and equals 1/4.

• Remember: π, e, √2, √3, √5 are irrational; every terminating or recurring decimal is rational.

question: If sinθ + cosθ = √6/2, then find tanθ + cotθ.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. 4.

GIVEN

• sin θ + cos θ = √6/2.

SOLUTION

• Square both sides: sin²θ + cos²θ + 2 sinθ cosθ = 6/4 = 3/2.

• 1 + 2 sinθ cosθ = 3/2, so sinθ cosθ = 1/4.

• tanθ + cotθ = (sin²θ + cos²θ)/(sinθ cosθ) = 1 ÷ (1/4) = 4.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

SHORT TRICK

• tanθ + cotθ = 1/(sinθ cosθ). Squaring the given relation gives sinθ cosθ = 1/4, so the answer is 4.

NOTE

• Option 1 (3), Option 3 (5) and Option 4 (6) are wrong: they would need sinθ cosθ = 1/3, 1/5 or 1/6, but squaring the given relation gives 1/4.

• Identities: (sinθ + cosθ)² = 1 + 2 sinθ cosθ; (sinθ – cosθ)² = 1 – 2 sinθ cosθ.

question:

The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. pasteurized.

◦ Example: All packaged milk is pasteurized before sale.

question:

question:
The following sentence has been divided into four parts. Identify the part which contains a grammatical error (ignore any punctuation error, if any). If there is no error in the sentence, then select 'No Error'.

(a) A large number of candidates who appeared for the civil services examination / (b) has expressed their concern regarding the unexpectedly high difficulty level / (c) of the newly introduced analytical section in the revised exam pattern. / (d) No error.
option_1: A large number of candidates who appeared for the civil services examination
option_2: has expressed their concern regarding the unexpectedly high difficulty level
option_3: of the newly introduced analytical section in the revised exam pattern
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. has expressed their concern regarding the unexpectedly high difficulty level.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The error is in part (b). The phrase "A large number of" is followed by a plural noun and takes a plural verb. Here the subject is "candidates", so the verb must be "have expressed", not "has expressed".

◦ Correct: A large number of candidates who appeared for the civil services examination have expressed their concern regarding the unexpectedly high difficulty level of the newly introduced analytical section in the revised exam pattern.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: Part (a) is correct: "A large number of candidates who appeared for the civil services examination" is a proper subject phrase.

 

• Option 3: Part (c) is correct: "of the newly introduced analytical section in the revised exam pattern" is a correct prepositional phrase.

 

• Option 4: "No error" is wrong, because part (b) has an error in subject–verb agreement.

 

NOTE

 

• Rule: "A large number of / a number of / a majority of" + plural noun takes a plural verb. But "The number of" + plural noun takes a singular verb (e.g. "The number of candidates is rising").

question:
Select the grammatically correct option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select 'No improvement'.

Although the library was very quiet, the student could not able to concentrate on his philosophy essay due to exhaustion.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. was not able to concentrate.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The underlined segment "could not able to concentrate" is wrong, because "could not" (a modal) must be followed by the base form of a verb, and "able" is an adjective that cannot follow a modal directly.

 

• The correct form is "was not able to concentrate" (or "could not concentrate"). (ध्यान लगाने में असमर्थ था)

◦ Correct: Although the library was very quiet, the student was not able to concentrate on his philosophy essay due to exhaustion.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 2: "could not concentrated" is wrong: a modal verb (could) is followed by the first form of the verb (concentrate), not the past form.

 

• Option 3: "cannot able to concentrate" is wrong: it is in the present tense, which does not suit the past tense of the sentence, and "cannot able" is not grammatical.

 

• Option 4: "No improvement" is wrong, because the underlined segment has an error.

 

NOTE

 

• Rule: be able to + V₁ (was/were/is able to), or modal + V₁ (could concentrate). Never use "modal + able to".

question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The girl said, “I can sketch a beautiful landscape.”
option_1: The girl said that she can sketch a beautiful landscape.
option_2: The girl said that she could sketch a beautiful landscape.
option_3: The girl said that I could sketch a beautiful landscape.
option_4: The girl said that she could sketched a beautiful landscape.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. The girl said that she could sketch a beautiful landscape..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In indirect (reported) speech, when the reporting verb ("said") is in the past tense, the tense of the reported speech shifts back: can → could. The pronoun "I" changes to "she" (the speaker, the girl).

◦ Correct: The girl said that she could sketch a beautiful landscape.

 

• Steps: (1) remove the quotation marks and put "that"; (2) change the pronoun to match the subject; (3) shift the tense back. (अप्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "…she can sketch…" is wrong: the tense of "can" is not changed to "could".

 

• Option 3: "…that I could sketch…" is wrong: the pronoun "I" is not changed to "she".

 

• Option 4: "…she could sketched…" is wrong: "could" must be followed by the base form (sketch), not the past form.

 

NOTE

 

• Tense changes in indirect speech: can → could, will → would, may → might, is/am/are → was/were, V₁ → V₂.

 

• Pronoun rule: first person follows the subject, second person follows the object, and the third person does not change.

question:

question:

question:
Select the correct direct form of the given sentence.

Mrs. Croft demanded to know who was speaking.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Mrs. Croft demanded, "Who is speaking?".

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The reported sentence is a question in indirect speech ("demanded to know who was speaking"). In direct speech, the reporting verb stays "demanded", and the past continuous "was speaking" returns to the present continuous "is speaking".

◦ Correct: Mrs. Croft demanded, "Who is speaking?"

 

• Steps: (1) keep the reporting verb "demanded"; (2) put the question in the original words inside quotation marks; (3) shift the tense one step forward (was speaking → is speaking), and use a question mark. (प्रत्यक्ष कथन)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1: "Who has speaking?" is wrong: it is ungrammatical, because "has" cannot be followed by "speaking" in this way, and "said" does not match "demanded".

 

• Option 2: "asked, 'Who was speaking?'" is wrong: the tense is not changed back to the present (is speaking), and "asked" changes the reporting verb.

 

• Option 3: "said, 'Who speaks?'" is wrong: it uses the simple present, which changes the sense from continuous to habitual, and "said" does not suit a question.

 

NOTE

 

• Tense changes when going from indirect to direct speech: was/were + V-ing → is/am/are + V-ing; V₂ → V₁; could → can; would → will.

question:
The sentences of a passage have been shuffled and labelled P, Q, R, and S. Rearrange these sentences to form the most logically coherent and meaningful paragraph. Choose the correct sequence from the options provided.

 

P: It has but established new classes, new conditions of oppression, new forms of struggle in place of the old ones.

 

Q: Society as a whole is splitting up into two great hostile camps, into two great classes, directly facing each other: Bourgeoisie and Proletariat.

 

R: Our epoch, the epoch of the bourgeoisie, possesses, however, this distinctive feature: it has simplified the class antagonisms.

 

S: The modern bourgeois society that has sprouted from the ruins of feudal society has not done away with class antagonisms.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. SPRQ.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The correct order is SPRQ.

 

• S is the opening sentence: it introduces the "modern bourgeois society" and says that it has not done away with class antagonisms. (वर्ग-विरोध)

 

• P follows S: "It has but established new classes…" The pronoun "It" refers to the bourgeois society in S, so P must come right after S.

 

• R comes next: "however, this distinctive feature: it has simplified the class antagonisms" develops the idea of antagonisms with the contrasting word "however", and brings in "our epoch".

 

• Q is the conclusion: "Society as a whole is splitting up into two great hostile camps…" It states the result of the simplified class antagonisms.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Option 1 (RSPQ) is wrong: R, with "however…", cannot start the paragraph, because "however" needs a statement before it.

 

• Option 2 (PRSQ) is wrong: P starts with the pronoun "It", which has no antecedent at the start of a paragraph.

 

• Option 3 (QSPR) is wrong: Q is a concluding statement about society splitting into two classes; it cannot be the opening sentence. (The PDF shows this option as a wrong selection.)

 

NOTE

 

• Tips for para-jumbles: (1) find the opening sentence that introduces the topic without pronouns; (2) match pronouns (it, this, they) with their nouns; (3) look for linkers such as however, but, thus; (4) the conclusion usually states a result.

 

• This passage is from The Communist Manifesto (Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, 1848).

The adult brain is more stable and less "malleable", which is beneficial for maintaining long-term memories but detrimental for the rapid acquisition of entirely new systems of thought. Learning a language at forty is a cognitive (D)____; at four, it is an effortless absorption.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.
